verdict: Parent and child. SP 800-171 is a set of requirements for nonfederal systems, drawn from the controls of SP 800-53.

rows.label: Purpose
rows.a: What a company outside government must do to protect controlled unclassified information.
rows.b: The catalog that federal systems choose their security and privacy controls from.

rows.label: Who Must Follow It
rows.a: Binds contractors through DFARS 252.204-7012, which a class deviation pins to Revision 2, and through CMMC.
rows.b: Federal information systems select from it under FISMA and OMB Circular A-130. Anyone else may use it.

rows.label: How It Is Assessed
rows.a: On its own it is self-attested. CMMC Level 2 assesses its 110 requirements.
rows.b: Assessors test the chosen controls with SP 800-53A procedures, and an authorizing official decides.

rows.label: Its Unit
rows.a: A requirement such as 03.01.01 in Revision 3, or 3.1.1 in Revision 2.
rows.b: A control such as AC-2, and enhancements such as AC-2(1).

connect: For each Revision 3 requirement NIST names the SP 800-53 controls it was drawn from. The count below is Revision 3’s: NIST’s export of Revision 2, the edition contracts still use, carries no such references.
noScore: Lensatic gives no strictness score here. One is a tailored selection of the other for a different kind of system, so neither is stricter in general.
overlapLine: Counted from NIST’s own references in Revision 3. Open a family to follow them down to each control.
